I take the central question from the title and opening: **Can solar radiation pressure (SRP) produce ‘Oumuamua’s observed non-gravitational acceleration, Δa ∝ r⁻² with a₀ ≈ 4.9×10⁻⁴ cm s⁻²?** Range: the observed arc near perihelion, not its whole history. Kind of question: *what produces it?*

**Jobs.** J1: why the acceleration is radial, ∝r⁻², of that size, not zero or other. *Given.* J2: why no comet tail or gas despite close approach. *Given.* J3: why no outgassing spin-up. *Given.* J4: why a very thin object survives interstellar travel. *Added.* J5: why it does not break from rotation or tides. *Added.* J6: why extreme aspect ratio/tumbling/pancake shape. *Given.* J7: why low thermal emission/high reflectivity. *Given.* J8: origin, natural or artificial. *Added, speculative.*

**Change list.** Change r from 0.25 AU outward; expect Δa ∝ r⁻². Change m/A: lower or higher changes acceleration and survival. Change C_R from 1 to 2 (absorber to reflector). Change density ρ from 1 to 3 g cm⁻³, which changes thickness. Change geometry: flat sheet, curved sheet, cone, ellipsoid; they say C_R stays order unity. Change ISM density ⟨n⟩ from 1 to 100 cm⁻³ and path L from 5 kpc to galactic. Change speed v from 26 km s⁻¹ to above 130 km s⁻¹. Change tensile strength from comet-like 10 dyne cm⁻² to diamond 2×10¹⁰. Change rotation period and tumbling. Change albedo α for area and mass. Change origin story.

**Parts and marks.**

| Part | Mark | Why |
|---|---|---|
| P1 SRP pressure P = C_R L⊙/(4πr²c) | **Held if** J2 and J3 are solid | Gives J1’s r⁻². But outgassing also gives r⁻². If the no-comet and no-spin-up jobs fail, P1 is only one route among rivals. |
| P2 required m/A ≈ 0.1 C_R g cm⁻² | **Held** by J1 | Swap m/A and the predicted acceleration moves. It is fixed by the observed a₀. |
| P3 thin sheet, 0.3–0.9 mm | **Loose** | Thickness depends on assumed density. The held part is “very small m/A”; the exact millimetres are free. |
| P4 area A ≈ 8×10⁶ α⁻¹ cm² and mass ≈740 kg | **Borrowed** from Jewitt et al. | Rests on the observed magnitude and albedo. It is not tested here. |
| P5 slow-down by ISM gas, Lmax ≈ 14 kpc | **Held if** J4 and ⟨n⟩ ≈ 1 cm⁻³ | At 100 cm⁻³ Lmax falls to ~0.14 kpc, so survival fails. The mark depends on the density assumed. |
| P6 dust vaporization limit, Lmax,d ≈ 330 kpc | **Held** by J4 but not limiting | It rules out vaporization as the blocker for m/A = 0.1. Numbers are loose, but it does a job. |
| P7 gas sputtering limit | **Idle** for the main claim | Removing it leaves the conclusion “survives” intact; it is a check that does not bind here. |
| P8 rotation stress | **Held** by J5 | Stress is far below even weak comet-like strength. Swap the material: still survives. |
| P9 tidal stress | **Held** by J5 | Negligible at perihelion; swap r and it grows only very close to a star. |
| P10 “natural, through a yet unknown process” | **Loose** catch-all | No gauge. It can absorb any failure. It needs something measurable that would show it swallowing a job. |
| P11 artificial lightsail or probe | **Borrowed** from Loeb 2018 and lightsail technology | Not tested here. It is a possible origin, not a working part of the acceleration explanation. |
| P12 C_R order unity for other shapes | **Loose** | They admit geometry changes C_R by order unity. That is a free parameter within the claim. |

**Whole-explanation checks.** *Flip:* if ‘Oumuamua had shown a comet tail, the paper would not back SRP in the same way; it would favour outgassing. So the story does not cover both outcomes. *Direction:* they infer m/A backward from the observed acceleration. That answers “what can we tell”, not “what produces it”. The production claim is SRP; the survival tests are forward from m/A. The mix is fair if the question is held. *Answer hidden?* m/A is not in the starting points, but the match to a₀ is set by choosing m/A. The added survival jobs J4–J5 constrain it. *Pairs that pull:* low m/A gives the observed acceleration; high m/A helps survive ISM slow-down. At 0.1 both pass for 5–10 kpc. Over ~14 kpc the pull would bite. *Catch-all:* the natural-origin clause has no gauge. *Change list leaves out:* exact shape, tumbling effect on C_R, full death of outgassing as a rival, the process that makes such a thin object. *Rivals:* outgassing is the main one; it also gives r⁻². They argue against it from no tail and no spin-up. A hidden subsurface source is not fully killed. *Where parts came from:* P1–P3 built from physics and the observed a₀; P4 borrowed; P5–P9 built; P10 asserted; P11 borrowed; P12 fitted to assumed geometry.

**What would make it harder to vary.** The main loose joint is P1. A phase-resolved test of the acceleration against ‘Oumuamua’s tumbling lightcurve would tighten it: if SRP is the cause, the acceleration should vary with projected area as it tumbles. If it does not, SRP is loose. A deeper non-detection of gas would also strengthen J2 and J3, which hold P1 in place.

**What this does not show.** Hard to vary is not true. The thin-sheet SRP story may still be false. Passing survival sums does not prove SRP drove the acceleration; it shows the object could survive if it were such a sheet. The artificial origin is speculation.

**One next step.** Check whether the non-gravitational acceleration varies with rotation phase in the way the projected area of a tumbling thin sheet would. That change would separate SRP from outgassing and either hold P1 or loosen it.
